claim: Architecture: the ratio ω₁/ω₂ is the primary inharmonicity gate — rational closes the scan into a (p,q) cable, irrational opens it into a Kronecker flow — so 'the boundary between harmonic and inharmonic is a continuous geometric parameter, not a categorical line' (Four Pillars Design Plan).

pieces.what: The torus with the scan path drawn live and heard: a ratio slider closes and opens the knot while the spectrum f = mω₁ + nω₂ lights its lattice. Tests whether the harmonic-to-inharmonic move is continuous by ear.
pieces.walks_up_from: one phasor on one circle: an ordinary 1D wavetable

pieces.what: The surface library as heard: each surface's image and its render side by side, nine voices from one scanning rule.
The built-but-unheard Hopf control surface, gathered as is, with the south pole (classic 1D wavetable) marked as the place to start.
The RMS dip: sine to sawtooth crossfaded linearly, then with constant-RMS, heard and plotted; tests the ~10 dB midpoint claim.
